lines: That is one thousand, four hundred and sixty hours a year.
You have a budget. It is not money.
It is twenty-four hours long, and it resets every morning.
Most of it is spoken for. One part is glowing: four hours, in this example.
Let us look at the books.
Here is an example day. Four hours in total.
On an iPhone, open Settings, then Screen Time.
On Android, open Settings, then Digital Wellbeing.
Hours per day, times three hundred sixty-five, divided by twenty-four, gives you full days per year.
Four hours a day is about sixty-one days. Over ten years, twenty months.
Rule three. Spend it on something.
Fourteen hundred and sixty hours could be about two hundred and forty books.
Or about two new languages, to a working level.
Or about seven thousand kilometres on foot.
These are estimates, to make the number real.
Rule four. Free is a price.
Nothing on this shelf costs money.
Each one costs about four hours a day.
You do not pay once. You pay every day.
Tool one. Mute everything that is not a person.
Sales, likes, news and game alerts each tap your shoulder.
Tool two. Charge the phone outside the bedroom.
Buy a cheap alarm clock. The last thing you see at night should not be a feed.
Tool three. Pause ten seconds before you open it.
Breathe. Ask what for. If you still want it, open it.
Tool four. Twenty, twenty, twenty, for your eyes.
Every twenty minutes, look at something twenty feet away, for twenty seconds.
Tool five. Stop at a time, not at the end of the feed.
There is no end of the feed. Pick a time, set an alarm, and let the day finish.
Two hours less screen. One walk. One book.
The rules: know your number, do the math, spend it on something, and remember, free is a price.
The tools: mute alerts, charge outside the bedroom, pause ten seconds, twenty twenty twenty, and stop at a time.
Screenshot this. Then tell me your number in the comments, and I will do the math.
Thank you for spending your time here.
